# Downstep

> Downstep is a free and open source (GPL-3.0) desktop app for Mac and Windows to practice music and learn songs by ear. It slows a song down without changing the pitch, changes the key without changing the speed, and loops the part you are learning (A-B loop). Songs stay on your computer, and it works offline.

- Price: free, no paid version, no account. Donations are optional.
- Platforms: macOS 11 or later on Apple silicon (M1 or later); Windows 10 and 11, 64-bit (beta). Intel Macs are not supported for now. No iPhone or Android version for now.
- Languages: English and Italian.
- Made by Damiano Giusti, a developer who plays guitar in a band. A free-time project.

## Features

- Speed from 25% to 200% without changing the pitch (time-stretching with the open source Bungee library), in 5% steps.
- Pitch from 12 semitones down to 12 semitones up without changing the speed, in 1 semitone steps.
- A-B loop: set A and B while the song plays or drag the markers; halve or double the loop; move it back or forward. Keyboard: Space play/stop, A and B set the loop, L loop on/off, arrows jump 5 seconds (1 with Shift).
- Each song keeps its own speed, pitch and loop. Named presets per song.
- Library: import MP3, M4A, WAV and FLAC files, or YouTube links (audio only, for content you have the rights to). Search and playlists.
- Sound: 7-band equalizer (60 Hz to 15 kHz), preamp, left and right balance.
- Export a song to MP3 with speed and pitch applied.
- Backup and restore of songs, presets and playlists, in the same format on Mac and Windows.
- The app updates itself when a new version is out.

## Good for

- Learning a guitar solo, a bass line, a drum fill or a vocal line by ear.
- Singers who need a song in a lower or higher key.
- Playing along with records tuned a half step down, in standard tuning.
- Bands that practice the same song in a different key at home.
- Musicians who want a free, open source alternative for slowing down and transposing audio on Mac or Windows.
